pages.title: Purpose
pages.text: The centrifuge reads the bee type recorded on a comb and turns combs and comb blocks into resources through Productive Bees recipes, often producing honey-like fluids as well. A plain centrifuge runs one operation at a time; Basic/Advanced/Elite/Ultimate factories run 3/5/7/9 in parallel.

pages.title: What "R" does
pages.text: The R button below the output slots returns the input slot as it is; it does not delete anything. With AE2 connected the items go back to the network, otherwise they are pushed along the Mekanism item output direction. Whatever cannot be returned stays in the input slot.

pages.title: Fluids and smelting
pages.text: In multi-fluid mode each fluid gets its own tank, and the Multi-Fluid Tanks tab lists the tanks other than the primary one. To smelt centrifuge raw ore into ingots, allow Smelting Compatibility in Machine Settings, install the Raw Ore Smelting Upgrade, then enable the F button on that centrifuge.

pages.title: Centrifuge-only switches
pages.text: The left column top to bottom: A = AE output; I = open the AE2 input window (pull from the ME network, Items page only); F = power furnace recipe compatibility; A = direct AE output (skips the local cache, rejects fall back); O = direct container output. A and I exist only with AE2 installed.

pages.title: Factories and logistics
pages.text: A factory packs a whole row of parallel slots into one block: one red input slot plus three blue output slots per process, one progress bar each, and one shared fluid tank. Higher tiers add parallelism, so power and output logistics must keep up.

pages.title: No progress?
pages.text: Use valid combs rather than honey bottles. Check FE, redstone mode, security and free space in every item slot and fluid tank. If only one fluid cannot leave, open the multi-fluid window and check whether that fluid's tank is full.
